notes: ZERO DISCRIMINATION: all 20 assertions pass in BOTH configurations (100% vs 100%). The pass rate measures nothing here; read the outputs, not the score.

Root cause for the two trap evals: the answers are already written into the source docstrings of asce7_22.py and nec_se_ds_2015.py, so the baseline reads the provision straight out of the code it is editing. That is a good property of the codebase and a fatal one for these evals.

Root cause for eval 3: both configurations independently cross-checked two pdftotext render modes, caught the merged-cell row-grouping trap, and stored the missing Ro as None rather than fabricating it. Extraction discipline was not the differentiator it was designed to be.

Qualitative difference the assertions do not capture: only the with_skill run on eval 1 verified the claim against the primary source (grep for 'Table 11.4' over the 7-22 PDF returns 0) and surfaced Commentary C11.4.3, which states the tables were eliminated. The baseline asserted the same conclusion from the docstring plus prior knowledge.
Cost: with_skill averaged +85k tokens (+29%) and +100s (+20%) per run. On eval 1 that bought a primary-source citation; on evals 2 and 3 it bought little that is measurable.

Both baseline runs found real defects in the library that neither trap assertion asked about: a silently-zero SDS on ASCE7_22 and two dead dataclass fields. Both have since been fixed. The eval surfaced more value as a code review than as a skill measurement.

Harness fault: isolation='worktree' seeded every agent from main (c00751e), not the working branch. Four agents self-corrected; the eval-3 baseline did not and had to be re-run pinned to bd20bec. Its first attempt is archived under _archived_invalid_baseline.

My first grading pass produced two false negatives from brittle keyword matching (it missed 'is correct - I did not change the code' and validation prose that lived in notes.md rather than response.md). Assertions were regraded against response + notes + patch combined.
